title: Ordered affine adjunctions give the integration transpose with the actual compositor
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $d\geq0$ put $X_d=\mathbf A^d_Y$ and $p_d:X_d\to Y$ [def-sbc-affine-space], with $X_0=Y$ and $p_0=1_Y$. Use the small pro-etale derived categories, derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the specified Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], compact supports [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$ and $\omega_f=Rf^!A_{\operatorname{target}(f)}$. The vector integration $t_f:Rf_!A_{\operatorname{source}(f)}(r)[2r]\to A_{\operatorname{target}(f)}$ for a rank-$r$ trivial bundle $f$ is [def-amb-vector-integration], realized on this site by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Write $P_{f,H}:Lf^*H(r)[2r]\to Rf^!H$ for the exceptional transpose of $(1_H\otimes t_f)\Pi_{f;A(r)[2r],H}$, where $\Pi_{f;M,H}:Rf_!(Lf^*H\otimes M)\to H\otimes Rf_!M$ is the inverse of the canonical compactification projection [def-exchange-projection], with tensor symmetries inserted.

Fix the coordinate order, put $q_m:X_{m+1}=\mathbf A^1_{X_m}\to X_m$ for the last-coordinate projection, so $p_{m+1}=p_mq_m$, and fix $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use on each ordinary etale base the explicit affine-line adjunction of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], composed in this order, with right adjoint $G_mK=p_m^*K(m)[2m]$ and with $G_0=1$. Let $F_m$ be its ordered compact-support left adjoint. Identify $F_m$ on bounded-below inputs with $Rp_{m!}$ by the normalized proper/open compactification compositor. Let $\alpha_m:Rp_{m!}Rq_{m!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{m+1,!}$ be precisely the compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition] on witnessed bounded-below etale-origin inputs.

For $f=q_m$, $g=p_m$, compactifying $g$ by $(\mathbf P^1_Y)^m$ and using a compatible compactification triangle for $f$, the ordinary-etale proper/open compositor is carried to this actual $\alpha_m$ under the proper and open site comparisons. For the canonical projection maps, with $P_u=Lu^*$ and the canonical tensor, pullback and direct-image associators, the maps satisfy
$$\operatorname{PF}_{gf;M,H}(\alpha_{m,M}\otimes1)=\alpha_{m,M\otimes P_fP_gH}\,Rg_!(\operatorname{PF}_{f;M,P_gH})\,\operatorname{PF}_{g;Rf_!M,H}.$$
They also satisfy the compactification tensor-action identity. On the bounded constructible, finite-Tor coordinate inputs the composite adjunction counit at every $K$ is
$$\varepsilon^{(m)}_K=(1_K\otimes t_{p_m})\Pi_{p_m;A(m)[2m],K},$$
where $t_{p_m}$ is precisely the ordered counit trace at $A_Y$ of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], and therefore the integration of [def-amb-vector-integration] in the trivial frame. The site comparisons identify these counits and their exceptional transposes.

On the pro-etale site let $c_m:Rp_{m+1}^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_m^!Rp_m^!$ be the right-adjoint conjugate of $\alpha_m$ and let $I_{m,K}$ be the pullback/twist-additivity source identification, both as specified in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]. For a line projection $f$ let $\Gamma_{f,H}$ be the transpose of $(1_H\otimes I_S)\Pi$, where $I_S$ is restriction by the open counit of the projective-line trace [def-amb-p1-trace], using the specified site realization. This defines the line maps at every $n\geq1$, without a divisibility restriction. Define the ordered maps by $\Gamma_{p_0,K}=1_K$ and
$$\Gamma_{p_{m+1},K}=c_m(K)^{-1}\circ\Gamma_{q_m,Rp_m^!K}\circ Lq_m^*(\Gamma_{p_m,K})(1)[2]\circ I_{m,K}.$$
Then
$$P_{p_m,K}=\Gamma_{p_m,K}\quad(m\geq0).$$
In particular this recursion uses the actual exceptional target $Rp_m^!K$, with $Rp_m^!K\cong G_mK$ via $P_{p_m,K}$; its line input lies in $D^b_{ctf}$. Under this identification the naturality square is
$$\Gamma_{q_m,Rp_m^!K}\,Lq_m^*(P_{p_m,K})(1)[2]=Rq_m^!(P_{p_m,K})\,\Gamma_{q_m,G_mK}.$$
All shifts in these source identifications are even. The rank-zero comparison is the identity and the formulas include $K=0$ and empty bases.

proof.text: The endpoint existence and uniqueness assertions are proved by explicit transport: identify the recursive affine towers and projections by induction, transport the ordinary trace, use the canonical coefficient-action comparison for the tensor source, and use dependent recursion for ordinary source descent. HEq determines each morphism uniquely; Iso.ext determines each isomorphism. These arguments also cover dimension zero.

For the coordinate hypotheses, N is invertible on the affine tower. The finite Tate-line theorem gives a locally constant free rank-one cover and exact tensoring. The finite-values criterion makes the line constructible. Its single complex, its shift by two, and the recursive tensor products lie in the ordinary constructible finite-Tor category. Pullback preserves that category; the realized tensor comparison supplies the literal pro-etale source origin. The bounded coefficient and finite-Tor input give the compared compactification projection formula; the two signed symmetries are isomorphisms. The proved coefficient_plus_on_base assertion uses the supplied structure map to ensure invertibility. It now supplies the boundedness argument of integration itself; the false unrestricted auxiliary coefficient_plus assertion is withdrawn. Proof irrelevance keeps the integration morphism unchanged.

First work on ordinary etale sites. Choose an annihilating power $N=\ell^a$ for $A$; it is invertible on every scheme here. The base and its affine and projective coordinate spaces are Noetherian: a field is Noetherian and apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to their finite-type structure maps. For the ordered compactifications use the product of projective lines specified in the statement. The ordinary-etale composition comparison is the proper/open tower comparison of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], whose bounded-below restriction is the specified ordinary comparison. The equation for $B_{gf}C(\alpha^e)$ in [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence] identifies it with the actual compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition], rather than an unspecified isomorphism of left adjoints. The latter theorem also keeps every bounded-below etale witness in its domain. This proves the first site/compositor assertion. The CoordinateCoherence site clause is a direct specialization of the already proved generic composition site square with the coordinate Noetherian instances.

proof.text: The compactification projection maps satisfy the displayed composition equation: on ordinary etale sites apply [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] to $f=q_m$, $g=p_m$, and insert tensor symmetry to put the coefficient on the right. Its statement includes the actual proper/open interchange and refinements. Transporting the specified projection maps is justified by [lem-pur-finite-site-counit-projection-transport], and the compositor by Step 3. Alternatively [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate] gives precisely the stated pro-etale equation on the compatible compactification triangle. The tensor-action identity, including its ordinary-etale version, is clause 3 of [lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws]. We use the ordinary equations before transporting the bounded inputs; no ambient pro-etale projection isomorphism is being inferred. The ordinary projections needed below are invertible on all inputs by [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection]. Thus inverse projections and every intermediate tensor expression in the next two steps are defined. The ordinary projection clause of CoordinateCoherence uses compactSupportProjectionMap_comp directly. Both tensor-action clauses specialize the proved generic compactification tensor-action laws at ModuleCat (AffineLinePurity.Ring P), without changing scalar rings or any source coordinates. The scalar tensor-action predicates are specializations of category-level definitions of their literal equations, so the generic law proofs share the derived tensor and inverse-image structures before specialization; no canonical map or hypothesis changes.

proof.text:
For a single coordinate line $f:S\times\mathbf A^1\to S$, write $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow P$ and $r:P\to S$. Put $W=A_P(1)[2]$. By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] the projective adjunction has counit $(1_H\otimes t_r)\Pi_r$ for every ordinary-etale $H$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], composition with $j_!\dashv j^*$ makes the affine counit equal to this map preceded by $Rr_*(\varepsilon_{j,r^*H\otimes W})$. Clause 2 of [lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws] rewrites this open counit, after the open tensor comparison, as $\varepsilon_{j,W}\otimes1_{r^*H}$. Naturality of the proper projection then gives
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{line}}_H=(1_H\otimes I_S)\Pi_f,\qquad I_S=t_r\,Rr_*(\varepsilon_{j,W}).$$
The canonical pullback identification of the twist is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Hence the line trace is exactly the restricted projective trace in [def-amb-p1-trace], and its exceptional transpose is the line map in the statement. This calculation applies to every finite $A$ killed by $N$; it uses no flatness over $\mathbf Z/N$ and imposes no divisibility condition on $n$.

source.place: Ordered product of rank-one orientations: normalization of each affine-line counit

proof.text: For ordinary_counit_formula, induct on the number of coordinates, universally quantifying the finite-Tor input K at each rank. The base case is lem-pur-affine-ordered-counit-zero. At rank d+1, specialize lem-pur-affine-ordered-counit-successor to the induction hypothesis for every K and its finite-Tor proof. The canonical sources and transported counits are the unchanged constructions in def-pur-affine-ordered-counit-data. This proves the original literal coefficient-counit equation without altering its hypotheses or maps.

source.place: Final paragraph, ordered affine-space integration and canonical reassociations; expanded ordered-transpose proof Steps 5 and 6.

proof.text: For the integration transpose use the one-coordinate identity of lem-pur-affine-ordered-integration-successor. Its dimension-zero value is the identity by the defining unique HEq characterization. Induct on d and substitute the induction hypothesis in the literal comparisonStep recursion to identify it with affineSpacePurityComparison. CoordinateLineAdjunction supplies invertibility of the affine-line map on the actual stage input. The inverse compositor is invertible because its Hom correspondence is a composite of the two relative adjunction bijections and the actual origin compositor. A second induction on the successor identity proves invertibility of the integration transpose. No general ambient pro-etale adjunction is used.

source.place: Canonical reassociations: transport of the actual counit and its transpose

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-affine-line-comparison-naturality on X_d to the actual arrow integrationTranspose_d, using source_applicability and stage_applicability for its two retained origins. This gives exactly the stated naturality square. Together with the two inductions, compositor invertibility, the successor step and the literal zero characterization, this assembles all six conjuncts. Rank zero, zero inputs and empty bases require no extra hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem ordered_integration_transposes (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY] [IsSeparated aY] (K : Plus (AffineLinePurity.Ring P) Y) (Ke : Etale.DerivedCategoryModule (AffineLinePurity.Ring P) Y) (hKe : etaleFiniteTor (AffineLinePurity.Ring P) Y Ke) (eK : (comparison (AffineLinePurity.Ring P) Y).obj Ke ≅ K.obj) : (∀ d : ℕ, integrationTranspose P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d = affineSpacePurityComparison P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, IsIso (integrationTranspose P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d)) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, IsIso (exceptionalComposite P Y aY K d)) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, integrationTranspose P Y aY K Ke hKe eK (d + 1) = (sourceReassociation P Y aY K.obj d).hom ≫ (lineSource P (iteratedAffineLine Y d)).map (integrationTranspose P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d) ≫ exceptionalLine P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d ≫ exceptionalComposite P Y aY K d) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, (lineSource P (iteratedAffineLine Y d)).map (integrationTranspose P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d) ≫ exceptionalLine P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d = sourceLine P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d ≫ (rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (AffineLinePurity.Ring P)) (lastProjection Y d)).map (integrationTranspose P Y aY K Ke hKe eK d)) ∧ HEq (integrationTranspose P Y aY K Ke hKe eK 0) (𝟙 K.obj)
